questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Oppurtunity to learn spanish and going to a culturally very different part of the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, the office at uniandes that helps exchange students is very good, and whenever there was something i couldn't figure out on my own i went to them, and they solved it or pointed me in the right direction.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Read the above

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I had a contact so therefore it was very easy. But my recommendation is to search online, and book a hostel for the first week or two. This means that you can ask around if your fellow students know a good place, and you can visit potential flats. 

The housing arranged through the uni is fine enough, but its expensive compared to other options, and you move in to flats with almost nothing (only a bed and lamps more or less) and have to buy all the stuff yourself. Besides, they are quite strict with visitors, so it can feel a bit like living in a hotel.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That the areas around uniandes not are the safest, but this is also where the official student accomodation is located. So maybe if you like it a bit more chill, find somewhere a bit more north of uni. (Although public transport can be a bit difficult - i would recommend investing in an old bike if you don´t live in walking distance to uni)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you go with the official housing then choose Central X over CityU. In cityU you cant open the windows properly and they are stricter with entrance and guests and so on.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: These things are always tedious and not necessarily very logical, but if you are lucky you can find someone who has been through them before and ask them. (And contact the helpoffice at uniandes as much as you feel like)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I honestly don´t remember

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classed i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for more classes than you need, you can drop the ones you have extra up until sometime in october. (So either take an extra few fun classes, or do it because you are in doubt which to choose)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I study anthropology but didn't do any anthropologycourses at uniandes, so i don't really know to be honest.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Many of the courses have smaller classes, which means its often more dialog teaching (which i really liked) but I think it depends a lot on the subject.

In general columbian students spend a lot of time on uni, and the culture is to be on campus most days and for many hours.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The spanish classes are great. I would especially recommend the intersemestrial one from start of juli that goes for a month. Its a great introduction to the uni, some of your new exchangemates, and the city in general. Even if you cant get credits for it, i would really recommend it!

The salsa classes are very fun (but you can also show up without being inscribed (shhhh))

questions.answer: All the traveling :))

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries are more expensive than i would have thought, but going out to eat (especially lunch menues) is cheap, and often cheaper than cooking on your own.

Uber/Indrive or whatever ride-app is very cheap, but you also probably need to use it a lot, and will be a decent part of your expenses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There are many clubs, but mostly very specific ones like astronomy or manga and stuff like that. 
The sports courses are very fun (even though the kind of are counted as academic)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dosens, but I never joined any of them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Salsa/dancing classes, also so that you dare to go out on salsabars (Columbians are mostly very good, but its still very fun and a good way to meet new people whos not from uni)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel as much as you can around in Columbia, its the greatest. My favorite place was the pacific coast, we went on the 1-week holiday in october and prolonged or vacation a bit :)) I would recommend to fly to Nuquí and visit towns from there, its the greatest. 

But do many weekendtrips! Go to Tatacoa-dessert, to Bucharamanga, to Los Llanos, Cali, Chiquinquirá, Villa de Leyva, Santander, places on the northcoast (you'll need more than a weekend), and the Amazon!!
There are also so many great places to hike in and near bogotá!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Bogotá is a very big and very busy city, with a lot of stuff going on everywhere. You will spend a lot of time in traffic, and you will probably think more about your security than you are used to in Europe. 
But the Colombians are great and helpful and friendly. And they love to party and to meet new people, so if you want you can easily make a lot of friends while you are there (especially if you speak some spanish).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Uniandes is the most expensive uni in the country, so most students come from very wealthy backgrounds. This often means that they like stuff like going to malls, and in general behaving a bit like they think american youth act. (and you usually starts uni when you are 17, so most people are quite young).
But you can definetly find people that stick out, you'll just have to approach them in your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Colombians don't usually make plans far out in the future, and if you made one you will have to confirm with them if its still there haha.
And they will often invite you to stuff, and then never follow up on it (unless you ask them later), but don't be offended, if you like them just ask them again. 
But yeah a lot of them will probably cancel on you once in a while. Most plans are made on the day it happens.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: As i said before, extremely sweet, funny, helpful, festive, open, and in general very curious about other cultures.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to avoid courses monday/friday, so its easier to go on long weekend trips :))

Bring extra credit card / phone from home. Its quite likely that you will lose it (stolen) at one point. 

Its very much worth it to go, even though its a bit unsafe and very different!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to talk with so many people in their native language made traveling a very different (and much better) experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The city of Bogotá will never be a place where i feel that much at home. Its to unsafe, noisy and grey. But the people make up for it of course.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
